title: Verifiable Attestation Portal + Pay-per-Export Pricing Pilot
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Goal: Build a customer-facing portal that generates cryptographically signed, auditable attestation packages (SIG/CAIQ-lite) on demand and experiment with a pay-per-export microbilling model. This pilot should reduce time-to-contract for sales, lower manual effort for security/reviews, and surface a price signal for heavy attestation consumers.

Scope: MVP portal + backend flow that: (1) accepts a customer request for a compact attestation pack (selected sections of CAIQ + normalized claims), (2) compiles supporting evidence links and sanitized config exports, (3) signs the resulting bundle using a Redwood-managed KMS key with an embedded audit log (who requested, template used, export timestamp), and (4) provides a single-click verifiable download along with a short human-readable cover summary.

Key differentiators & product choices (trade-offs considered):
- Verifiable credentials (W3C VC) vs. simple PDF + signature: we prefer W3C VC JSON-LD for machine verification but will provide a PDF snapshot for legal teams. This increases engineering work but enables downstream automation for customers.
- Pay-per-export microbilling vs. included in enterprise package: pilot will introduce a low per-export fee and a monthly export allowance for enterprise contracts. This allows measurement of true operational cost and monetization while preserving negotiated terms.
- CAIQ-lite generation: rather than attempting to always provide full SIG/CAIQ, we will map a curated set of 30 high-value sections to templated claims + links to existing evidence. This reduces legal review cycles but will require a review matrix to ensure accuracy.
- Caching & search: store generated responses and index them to allow reuse (with TTL) for repeat customer requests. We will keep a TTL of 90 days to balance freshness with savings.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
1) Portal UI where customers (or SEs) can request an attestation pack and select from predefined templates.
2) Backend that assembles the pack (claims + evidence links + sanitized config snippets) and creates a signed artifact using KMS.
3) Downloadable package exposes a JSON-LD verifiable credential, a human-readable cover PDF, and a verifiable signature URL.
4) Audit log entry created for each export with requestor identity, template ID, and export hash; log is queryable by support and security.
5) Billing event emitted for exports (both allowance consumption and pay-per-export) and visible in customer billing UI.
6) Legal + Security review sign-off checklist completed for templates and sample exports.

Non-goals for MVP: automated per-question generation for full CAIQ; on-prem private signing (will be considered in Dedicated/Private roadmap).

Metrics to evaluate pilot: number of exports/week, median time from request to delivery, number of follow-up manual evidence requests, revenue generated by exports, and downstream sales velocity for contracts that used the portal.

Risks & mitigations:
- Incorrect claims selected -> require mandatory Security/Legal gating for changes to templates and a visible template change history.
- Leakage of secrets in config exports -> implement sanitization heuristics and enforce review for any template that includes exportable config.
- Customer confusion about what is legally binding -> include clear human-readable disclaimers and a versioned archive of each generated artifact.

Next steps: finalize template matrix with Security and Legal; prototype signing flow with KMS and produce 5 sample exports for review; wire billing events into billing pipeline for telemetry (no invoice changes in pilot).
